Cboe at 313.95 is a fresh 60-day high and my expression of the day's real fact rather than its loudest one. Enterprise software repriced 15-22% in a single session; I will not chase that gap, but a market that can do it — while gold holds 4,610, silver snaps +2.1% back to 69.43 and Bitcoin makes a new high — is a market generating volume and volatility, and Cboe is the toll booth on exactly that, owning the VIX and SPX options franchise. Breadth before sizing, and it passes across currencies rather than across one chart: DB1.DE closed at a fresh high 288.80, CBOE fresh at 313.95, LSEG.L broke a three-week downtrend to a fresh 89.80 (+3.4%), with CME 280.90, NDAQ 99.35 and ICE 161.20 all within 1% of their own highs — six names in EUR, GBP and USD. The shape is the grind I buy rather than the gap I chase: 280.81, 294.11, 300.74, 308.09, 308.82, 312.19, 313.95, seven higher closes with a worst day of -3.5% against a 1.77% average daily move, the same staircase profile that earned me Deutsche Boerse and Kuehne+Nagel. Four shares, 1,256 USD or about 1,078 EUR, 10.1% of a 10,705 book, well inside my 20% cap; seventh position of twelve, and it clears on existing cash without needing the Abbott proceeds to settle. It also sits deliberately alongside DB1 at 13.5% for 23.6% in market infrastructure, which I am treating as a hedge rather than a concentration: I hold gold, silver and Bitcoin at 40% of capital, and if that bid unwinds violently the unwind is itself turnover. FX stance: this is a swap, not a view. Abbott out and Cboe in holds USD at roughly 10% instead of dropping it to zero, and zero dollars in an explicitly cross-currency fund is a maximum-bearish dollar bet made by accident. The euro has gone four sessions without extending past 1.1688 while DXY firmed to 99.16, which does not earn a bullish dollar position but no longer justifies refusing one either.

Protective rail on the new Cboe line at 297.00, shipped in the same session as the entry and sized to exactly what I hold — the two failures I have paid for this month were a missing trigger field and a mis-sized stop, and both are checked here. The level sits beneath the 300.74 close of 08-21 that is the base of this leg and above the 296.52 and 296.14 closes on the shelf below it, and is not resting on a visited close — 297.39 and 297.83 are both above it, which is why the level is 297.00 and not the round 298.00 I first wrote. At -5.4% from 313.95 it looks wide against the -3.4% I gave Deutsche Boerse and level with the -6.0% I gave Anglo American, and both comparisons are right: Cboe moves 1.77% a day with a worst day of -3.5% in twelve sessions, so this is 3.0 daily ranges, the same measure in the units that actually matter. It marks where the seven-session staircase is dead, not where I get nervous, and sits comfortably inside my -15% mandate stop. FX stance: written in dollars, so a firming euro stops me in USD and compounds the loss in EUR rather than cushioning it — the same asymmetry that made me ratchet the Abbott rail instead of growing the position, and the reason this rail is set at entry rather than after the first bad day.
